\vspace{-3cm}

The data in this class activity comes from a study on residents of Framingham, MA, which was conducted to research variables related to heart health. We will work with a subset of the data, containing

* `cigsPerDay`: The number of cigarettes smoked per day during the study period.
* `education`: 1 = High School, 2 = Some College, 3 = College Degree, 4 = Advanced Degree.
* `male`: 1 = Male, 0 = Female.
* `age`: The age of the individual in years.
* `diabetes`: 1 if the individual has diabetes, 0 otherwise.

While the data were originally collected to study heart health, in this activity we will try to model the number of cigarettes smoked.

## The model

To account for excess zeros in the data, we fit a *zero-inflated Poisson* (ZIP) model. Here is the probability function for our model:

$$P(Y_i = y | \mathbf{x}_i) = \begin{cases} e^{-\lambda_i}(1 - p_i) + p_i & y = 0 \\ \dfrac{e^{-\lambda_i} \lambda_i^y}{y!}(1 - p_i) & y > 0 \end{cases}$$

where

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log \left( \frac{p_i}{1 - p_i} \right) &= \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\gamma} \\
\log(\lambda_i) &= \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta}
\end{aligned}
$$

## Model output

```{r include=F}
library(pscl)
library(tidyverse)

heart_data <- read.csv("~/Documents/Teaching/applied_glms/sta214-f26.github.io/class_activities/framingham.csv")

heart_data <- heart_data |>
  drop_na(male, age, education, diabetes, cigsPerDay, BMI) |>
  mutate(education = as.factor(education))
```

```{r}
m1 <- zeroinfl(cigsPerDay ~ male + age + education + diabetes, 
               dist = "poisson", data = heart_data)

summary(m1)
```
